name: Ehrwalder Alm
kurzbeschreibung: The Ehrwalder Alm at 1,500 metres at the foot of the Wetterstein mountains is a panoramic alpine plateau offering breathtaking Zugspitze vistas.
beschreibung:
Overview

The idyllic Ehrwalder Alm sits at approximately 1,500 metres above sea level upon a sun-drenched plateau nestled beneath the Wetterstein mountain range above Ehrwald. Framed by the monumental rock faces of the Zugspitze, Sonnenspitze, and Mieming Range, this alpine terrace ranks among the most beloved destinations in the Tiroler Zugspitz Arena. During summer, the plateau bursts into vibrant colour with lush pastures, rustic mountain chalets, and crystal-clear high-altitude lakes such as Seebensee and Drachensee. In winter, the area becomes a sunny, snow-reliable ski resort featuring perfectly groomed pistes, ski lodges, and a floodlit toboggan run. Its unique blend of alpine grandeur, modern cable car infrastructure, and warm Tyrolean hospitality captivates visitors year-round.

Route & Requirements

The Ehrwalder Alm can be reached comfortably by gondola, on foot, or by mountain bike. The modern 8-seater Ehrwalder Almbahn cable car whisks hikers, families with pushchairs, and wheelchair users smoothly from the valley to the plateau. Those preferring to walk can follow the scenic forest path or access road in roughly one hour of steady uphill walking. On the plateau, flat walking trails offer relaxed circuits between huts. For extended hikes to Lake Seebensee, Coburger Hütte, or the Tajakante via ferrata, sturdy hiking boots, weather protection, and alpine experience are essential.

Visiting & Getting There

The Ehrwalder Almbahn valley station is situated on the eastern edge of Ehrwald, easily reached toll-free via the B179 Fernpass route and L71 from Austria and Bavaria. Complimentary regional guest buses run frequently from Ehrwald railway station directly to the gondola terminal. Extensive free car parking is available at the lift base. The cable car and mountain restaurants operate from mid-May through early November in summer, and from December through April for the winter season.

Tips

Take the classic hike from the mountain station to emerald-green Lake Seebensee, celebrated as one of the most picturesque alpine lakes in the Alps. Directly by the top station, the Tirolerhaus restaurant features a spacious sun terrace, deckchairs, and authentic Tyrolean cuisine. During winter evenings, enjoy the thrilling 3-kilometre floodlit natural toboggan run leading back down to the valley.
